source_text: CAPUT DECIMUM SEPTIMUM, De fidei Christianae consequentibus et effectis: ubi de unione fidelium cum Deo, eorumque iustificatione Euangelica. Sequitur ex fide in Christum iustificatio, sanctificatio, et pax conscientiae. Hic de unione et iustificatione; de sanctificatione et pace sequentibus capitibus.
english: CHAPTER SEVENTEEN. On the consequences and effects of Christian faith: where on the union of believers with God, and their evangelical justification.
From faith in Christ follow justification, sanctification, and peace of conscience. Here union and justification; sanctification and peace in the chapters that follow.

source_text: II. Unio fidelium cum Deo est, qua homo Deo Patri, Filio et Spiritui Sancto, per fidem mystice quidem, vere tamen arctissime coniungitur, ut in eo maneat et beetur aeternum (Hos. 2:19-20; John 14:23; 17:21; Eph. 3:17; 1 Cor. 6:19). III. Notabilia: 1. Unio non est imaginaria sed vera—Deus venit, habitat, manet in homine. 2. Extra unionem homo neque bene agere neque vera tranquillitate frui neque beari potest (John 15:4-5). 3. Unio infirmitates in hac vita non omnino tollit, tamen tegit magis magisque purgat. 4. Quemadmodum fideles unum sunt cum Deo per Christum, ita inter se communionem bonorum habent.
english: II. The union of believers with God is that by which a human is joined to Father, Son, and Holy Spirit through faith—mystically yet truly and most closely—so as to abide in Him and be blessed forever.

Notabilia: the union is real not imaginary; outside it one can neither act well, enjoy true peace, nor be blessed; it does not wholly remove infirmities in this life yet covers and increasingly purges them; believers united to God also share communion with one another.

source_text: IV. Unionem cum Deo per fidem sequitur IUSTIFICATIO EVANGELICA, quae est actus gratuitae gratiae, qua Deus peccatorem propter solum Christi meritum fide apprehensum a reatu absolvit et iustum reputat (Rom. 3:24-28; 4:5; 5:1; 2 Cor. 5:21). Opponitur in actu iustificationis proprium meritum et operatio.
english: IV. Union with God through faith is followed by EVANGELICAL JUSTIFICATION: an act of free grace by which God absolves the sinner from guilt and reckons him righteous solely for Christ's merit apprehended by faith.
In the act of justification one's own merit and working are opposed.

source_text: 1. Gratia qua iustificamur non est qualitas sive donum nobis infusum atque inhaerens, sed ipsa Dei misericordia et favor in Christo. 2. Gratia non est prorsus absoluta sed determinata ad Christi meritum. 3. Fides, etiamsi nunquam sola est sed bonis operibus tanquam fructibus stipatur, sola tamen iustificat. 6. Iustificatio hominis conversi tam diu durat quamdiu eius vita et fides. 7. Iustitia fidei est ipsius Christi iustitia et inexhausta Dei gratia, quae solam consolationem parit. CAPUT DECIMUM OCTAVUM sequitur, De sanctificatione et bonis operibus.
english: 1. The grace by which we are justified is not an infused inherent quality but God's mercy and favor in Christ. 2. That grace is not utterly absolute but determined to Christ's merit.

3. Faith, though never alone but accompanied by good works as fruits, nevertheless alone justifies. Justification of the converted lasts as long as life and faith. The righteousness of faith is Christ's own righteousness and God's inexhaustible grace—the only true consolation.
CHAPTER EIGHTEEN follows, On sanctification and good works.
